input:
A centrifugal pump is used to move water between two vessels that are located at grade, and the duty point is essentially determined by the demand of the receiving vessel. At the duty point, the flow is 54 m3 h-1 against a head of 43 m, with a pump efficiency of 73%. The shaft power at the duty point is 8.7 kW. It is worth noting that the motor is rated 15% above the shaft power, which means that the installed rating provides a comfortable margin over the duty requirement rather than merely meeting it exactly.

The acceptance test was carried out at the duty point only, over a period of 4 h, and it is important to note that no cavitation was observed at any point during the test. This result, however, only covers the tested condition and nothing beyond it. Operation away from the duty point was not tested, and the suction behaviour at other flow rates therefore rests on the pump curve rather than on any direct test evidence. Within the tested condition, the pump can be said to meet the duty as specified; outside that condition, the duty figures should be regarded as specification values rather than as measured performance, and the margin in the motor rating is a margin against the specified power, not against a measured one.
